react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on galactose metabolism (KEGG:map00052 / KEGG:hsa00052) as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned this KEGG map at rank 2 with an FDR of 8.76e-15 and a fold-enrichment of 1453, driven by sucrose, galactitol, galactinol, myo-inositol, and glycerol. MetaboAnalystR PSEA independently identified the human-specific ortholog KEGG:hsa00052 as the top hit with p=5.65e-09, matching the same five compounds. Mummichog's empirical m/z network ranked galactose metabolism fourth (p=0.007) with an 11-of-12 metabolite overlap, confirming the signal through mass-distance inference even when formal ID resolution is noisy. The five driver metabolites share no InChIKey structural conflicts (reconcile_inchikey confirmed five distinct block-14 clusters), ruling out namespace artefacts. Sucrose (C00089) is the pathway entry substrate cleaved by invertases to release glucose and fructose; galactinol (C01235) is the raffinose-family donor that transfers galactose to myo-inositol via galactinol synthase. Galactitol (C01697) accumulates as the toxic product of aldose reductase when galactose flux is high, a hallmark of classic galactosemia biochemistry. Glycerol (C00116) appears in both galactose metabolism and glycerophospholipid biosynthesis, consistent with its dual-role as a central carbon skeleton and membrane-lipid precursor. Aspirin (C01405) is flagged by RaMP as a member of the broader 'Metabolism of lipids' Reactome module, reflecting salicylate's known perturbation of phospholipid remodelling. Methionine sulfoxide (C02989) and allysine (C04076) remain pathway-peripheral, without strong enrichment in any single paradigm, suggesting oxidative-stress and collagen-crosslinking context that may be contextual to the treatment rather than a core pathway driver.
